mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport/civil-registry authority of the partner's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, directors, senior officers, and beneficial owners against Canadian FINTRAC PEP lists, United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, Her Majesty's Treasury (UK) sanctions, EU consolidated sanctions, and Alberta/Canadian domestic law-enforcement watchlists. Enhanced due diligence required for any non-Canadian resident partner from high-risk or monitored jurisdictions; continuous monitoring and re-screening at minimum every 90 days and upon any change in partners or UBO composition. Written risk assessment and compliance program must be implemented prior to registration and maintained for the life of the limited partnership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Service Alberta Corporate Registry (authorized NUANS search through alberta.ca/corporate-registry or licensed service agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the official registration language for Alberta. A partnership name may include French where so chosen; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters. The legal name must include the statutory entity designator 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', or 'LP' as permitted under the Partnership Act. Transliteration and language conventions must be approved by the Corporate Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A written objection or administrative appeal must be filed with the Director of Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, within 30 days of the conditional refusal. The submission must demonstrate: (i) distinguishability from existing registrations; (ii) compliance with the Partnership Act naming regulations; and (iii) where rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, submission of prior ministerial consent, written authorization from the regulating professional body, or trademark-holder consent. If the administrative appeal fails, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Alberta Court of King's Bench.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted solely for the statutory registered-office address, process-service capacity, and registered-agent purposes. A virtual office does not satisfy municipal operating-premises licensing requirements for the ghost-kitchen business activity; an actual commercial kitchen suite with health, building, fire, and zoning permits is mandatory for delivery-only food operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: HIGH: Unannounced municipal public-health and food-safety inspections are expected at least twice per year during the first 12 months of operation. Alberta Health Services and municipal fire services conduct routine unannounced compliance checks on commercial food-production and delivery-only facilities; probabilistic risk is approximately 70% in the initial operating year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), especially s 51 and registration provisions under s 73; Partnerships Regulation AR 133/2010.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), Corporate Registry Operations
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or deposit account requirement for an Alberta limited partnership; capital contributions are fixed in the partnership agreement and may be payable in cash, property, services, or on call as agreed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of the limited partnership hereby adopts the executed Partnership Agreement and causes the preparation, execution, and filing of the Declaration of Limited Partnership with the Alberta Corporate Registry under the Partnership Act (Alberta). The registered office of the partnership shall be the address set forth in the filing, and the Corporate Registry shall be promptly notified of any future change. The subscribing General Partner is appointed first Managing General Partner, with full power and authority to select banking institutions, open operational accounts, and execute delivery-platform agreements. A second partner is appointed Compliance Officer, authorized to obtain food establishment permits and statutory registrations. Any further ministerial acts to give effect to these resolutions are hereby approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation with the Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Registry online portal or licensed registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate/limited partnership name search in the Alberta Corporate Registry database. Submit the proposed name, including the term 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP', together with the prescribed reservation request. The reservation, if approved, is valid for 90 days and must be used within that window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to confusing similarity or non-distinctiveness, file an administrative review with Service Alberta within 30 days of the notice or submit a revised name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel and notary public engaged by the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a limited partnership agreement identifying each general and limited partner, capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, transfer restrictions, dissolution events, and Alberta governing law. Execute the agreement before a notary, retain the original in the registered records, and make certified copies available for financial institution onboarding.
required_dossiers: Proof of residential or business address for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar or a banking partner challenges any term, circulate a curative written consent signed by all partners and attach it as an amendment to the partnership agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration of Limited Partnership and Pay Prescribed Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry counter or electronic registry agent portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the statutory Declaration of Limited Partnership to the Registrar, verifying that the name, general partner name, and physical Alberta registered office address are exact. Pay the prescribed registration fee and request the Certificate of Registration for banking and licensing purposes.
required_dossiers: Authorizing signatures of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, correct the stated deficiencies and file an amended Declaration within 30 days; expedited correction may be available through a licensed registry agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for CRA Business Number and Provincial Account Enrolments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; Alberta WCB and municipal business licence offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Registration, apply for a CRA Business Number and select program accounts for GST/HST and payroll where employees will be engaged. Register separately for Alberta Workers' Compensation Board coverage and the municipal business licence required for food preparation facilities.
required_dossiers: Identification of the managing partner or officer
Registered office address and business contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the enrolment due to name or date mismatch, call the CRA Business Window with the registration document and resubmit through an authorized representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Governance Resolutions and Establish Banking Arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Managing General Partner and appointed officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting or execute unanimous written consent of the general partner to adopt the first board resolution, approve the banking resolution, and delegate authority for opening operational accounts. Preserve all execution copies in the partnership's minute book with the Certificate of Registration and partnership agreement.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or unanimous written consent
Identification of partner/officer signing the bank resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any banking or governance formalities are found deficient, pass a subsequent ratifying written resolution confirming the prior acts and update the minute book accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Health Services – Environmental Public Health Division; municipal business licensing authority such as City of Calgary Licence and Permit Services or City of Edmonton Licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Establishment Permit under the Public Health Act and the Alberta Food Regulation, supplemented by a municipal Business Licence for food service premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment; a Registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act may be required only if the facility adds food processing or significant wastewater discharge beyond the de minimis threshold. Otherwise, municipal wastewater approval is sufficient.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Kitchen wastewater must meet municipal sewer by-law parameters, including oil and grease limits, typically requiring grease traps and licensed grease-interceptor maintenance; cooking exhaust and odorous VOCs must comply with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives; all solid waste and grease waste disposal must be documented under applicable waste management regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and life safety inspection certificate from the local fire authority, structural load review for commercial ventilation and delivery-platform equipment, clearance under Alberta occupational health and safety requirements for on-site staff, and proof of food-handler sanitation training where required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (MyBA) portal; Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) for the statutory registration of the Limited Partnership
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident establishing an Alberta Limited Partnership must: (1) register the LP with the Alberta Corporate Registry under the Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c L-8, filing the required LP declaration and obtaining the Alberta registration/file number; (2) apply to the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) and a Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) account (account prefix RT), plus any payroll (RP) account, using Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1; the general partner must identify all non-resident partners and the foreign address of the partnership; (3) if the LP is a non-resident person carrying on business in Canada, comply with CRA non-resident registration requirements, including the appointment of a Canadian representative for service of documents where applicable; (4) receive the CRA Confirmation of Registration and use the BN in all GST/HST filings, export documentation, platform onboarding, and customs processes; (5) maintain CRA records and books for at least six years.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the Alberta Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c.1 (5th Supp.), s. 96; the partnership itself is not an income taxpayer and each partner, including non-resident partners, is taxable on its allocated share of income. For GST/HST purposes, the LP is a deemed 'person' under the Excise Tax Act, s. 123(1) as extended to partnerships, and may itself be a registered supplier carrying on a commercial activity in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; tax classification follows the facts and statute. Available statutory elections for the LP class include: (i) Income Tax Act s. 97(2) and s. 85(2) rollover elections on a tax-deferred transfer of eligible property into the partnership; (ii) Income Tax Act s. 249.1 election to adopt a non-calendar-year partnership fiscal period; (iii) Excise Tax Act Part IX elections relevant to cross-border and zero-rated supplies, including simplified documentation elections for exporters and the election to self-assess/rebate GST/HST on imported services; and (iv) for US-resident partners, the US federal check-the-box election (Form 8832) may independently determine the LP's US classification. Hybrid mismatch treatment is mandatory under Canada's implementation of OECD BEPS Action 2 rules and does not require or permit an election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15, as amended; Alberta imposes the federal 5% GST only and has no provincial sales tax (no PST and no provincial component of HST). Prepared food and beverages sold through the ghost kitchen's delivery platform are taxable restaurant supplies, subject to GST at 5% in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies made in Canada (small supplier threshold, Excise Tax Act s. 148(1)(d)); registration is mandatory for a non-resident or domestic person carrying on a commercial activity in Canada whose taxable supplies exceed the threshold. Once registered, the LP must charge, collect, and remit 5% GST on its taxable supplies of prepared meals and delivery-support services unless a zero-rated export supply applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no continuous transaction control (CTC) system, and no digital stamping requirement. E-invoicing is voluntary under the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing framework (Peppol BIS 3.0). However, the LP must issue GST/HST compliant invoices containing all prescribed information under Excise Tax Act s. 221 and retain electronic books, records, and source documents for at least six years under ETA s. 286; CRA may require electronic records to be made available in readable format during audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is claimable when the ghost kitchen/cloud kitchen makes a qualifying export supply of goods under Excise Tax Act ss. 21-23 and Schedule VI, Part I, or a service supplied to a non-resident recipient under Part V, provided the supplier is the exporter-in-fact: title and risk of loss must pass to the foreign recipient, the goods must be physically shipped from Canada to a destination outside Canada, and contemporaneous commercial evidence must prove the foreign destination and settlement. Merely supplying goods through a domestic delivery aggregator to a foreign delivery address, without proper export evidence, does not qualify for the 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) validated export declaration (B13A / Canada Automated Export Declaration (CAED) electronic export report), including the courier/consolidator proof of export where applicable
Commercial invoice with applicable Incoterms showing that title and risk of loss transferred to the foreign recipient
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or carrier export manifest evidencing final destination outside Canada
Foreign purchase order or food-delivery platform settlement order (e.g., UberEats Marketplace Export Settlement, DoorDash Export Reconciliation) attaching the foreign jurisdiction
Proof of foreign currency settlement, including the inward remittance certificate or platform payout record referencing the foreign bank account
CRA zero-rating schedule or export declaration certificate prepared at the time of supply, if requested by the CRA auditor
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may deny zero-rating retroactively and reassess the supply at 5% GST with statutory interest if export documentation is missing, incomplete, or contradicted by the transactional evidence. A false zero-rating claim can attract civil penalties for false statements and negligence under Excise Tax Act ss. 280 and 285, the extension of the normal four-year reassessment period where misrepresentation is attributable to carelessness, neglect, or fraud (Income Tax Act s. 152(4)), and criminal tax evasion prosecution under Income Tax Act s. 239 and the corresponding Excise Tax Act offence provisions. The LP and its general partner remain jointly and severally liable for GST/HST collections and may be required to refund uncollected GST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as central monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential banking supervision; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for anti-money laundering and cross-border currency transaction reporting. Canada does not maintain a separate foreign-exchange control administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible. Canada maintains no meaningful distinction between current-account and capital-account convertibility and imposes no exchange-control approvals for foreign direct investment or repatriation of capital and after-tax profits. An Alberta Limited Partnership may receive capital contributions from non-residents, hold foreign-currency accounts in Canada, and remit distributions and profit shares abroad without central bank licensing. The only structural hurdles are Canadian withholding taxes under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, GST/HST compliance, and FINTRAC mandatory reporting of large cross-border electronic funds transfers equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 or equivalent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable in Canada. There is no statutory timeline for export proceeds surrender and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in CAD or any foreign currency. However, all receipts from goods or services, including delivery-platform payouts from foreign platform entities, must be included in the partnership’s taxable income and, where applicable, reported for GST/HST. Any wire transfer equal to or above the prescribed FINTRAC threshold must be reported by the financial institution.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Canada has no bank authorization regime for offshore EMI or fintech-issued IBAN accounts; only banks and provincial credit unions may accept deposits. Offshore payment fintechs may act as payment service providers or money services businesses but must comply with the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), and must register with FINTRAC when carrying on MSB activity in Canada. Virtual IBAN and platform payout services are viable as supplementary settlement conduits for UberEats and DoorDash payouts, but they must not be the sole treasury infrastructure. The Alberta LP should maintain primary operating and escrow balances at a Schedule I bank and use fintech rails only for pass-through disbursements with zero float retention.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement mandates that directors or partners appear in person for corporate account opening in Canada. Schedule I banks apply a risk-based AML/KYC approach; remote electronic KYC (eKYC) and video interview are often accepted for low-risk Canadian commercial entities. For an Alberta Limited Partnership with non-resident limited partners or unusual ownership layers, a physical interview or an enhanced video interview with the general partner and signatories is operationally required by major banks before issuance of a cheque-book, card, or online banking privileges. Evidence of registered Alberta office and a valid business address in Alberta remains mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership structure comprising non-resident limited partners and layered partnerships
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational chart; executed limited partnership agreement; Alberta Corporate Registry certified LP extract; register of partners and percentage interests; UBO declaration for all beneficial owners holding 10% or more; tax residency certificates; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements; CPA confirmation letter; signed indemnity and corporate KYC questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ghost-kitchen virtual-brand model with no physical storefront and high delivery-platform payout velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial kitchen lease or licensed commissary agreement; Alberta food service licence; municipal business licence; UberEats and DoorDash merchant agreements showing merchant IDs and payout cycles; sample payout statements; explanation of virtual-brand ownership and revenue recognition; documented control framework for customer refunds and chargebacks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injections from non-resident investors into an Alberta LP with mixed-currency flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreements and capital call notices; bank statements of the original funding accounts; LP cash-journal and capital-contribution ledger; tax identification numbers for all non-resident partners; evidence of economic substance in Alberta; declaration of source of funds; signed AML questionnaire; beneficial ownership registers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name screening match, adverse media, or international sanctions/politically exposed person (PEP) alerts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening reports from a recognized screening system; corporate registry searches; negative-media search results; non-PEP declaration and explanation of any identity matches; source-of-wealth documentation; legal opinions for complex cross-border funding; continuous transaction-monitoring undertaking.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident investors shall transfer capital contributions by SWIFT MT103 from their banking institution to the Alberta LP’s designated Canadian dollar account. The SWIFT payment message must include the investor’s legal name, the originating account number, and remittance narrative: 'LP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – [INVESTOR NAME] – ALBERTA LP [REGISTRY NUMBER]'. Canada does not assign government purpose codes; banks rely on the reason-for-payment/remittance narrative for AML and tax classification. Incoming CAD wires settle irrevocably via Payments Canada’s Large Value Transfer System (LVTS). US-dollar or FX proceeds may be credited to a segregated USD account converted at the bank’s FX desk. For any transfer equal to or above CAD 10,000 or equivalent, the receiving bank files a Large Cash Transaction/EWT report to FINTRAC. Onboarding verification dossier: executed subscription agreement; capital call; LP agreement; Alberta LP registration certificate; general partner resolution authorizing account signatories; partnership register; UBO list; source-of-funds evidence; signed indemnity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 with Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference (UETR) for traceability. For import of packaging, kitchen equipment, or food ingredients requiring payment security, the Canadian bank may issue a Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 to the foreign beneficiary. For high-value domestic CAD payments to suppliers and landlords, use LVTS. For recurring small-value obligations, payroll, and utility payments, use Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) or standard EFT ACH transactions. For marketplace payouts from UberEats and DoorDash, settlement instructions should point to the LP’s dedicated operational account; platform payouts are received via ACH/EFT or payment-processor rails and then reconciled against merchant IDs. All disbursements must be supported by invoices, delivery evidence, or service agreements, and must not create an un documented fundraising or consult fee pattern that would trigger enhanced transaction monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts executed with a licensed Schedule I bank or registered investment dealer
Cross-currency swaps matching non-resident investor capital contributions and repatriation/distribution timelines

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the counterparty is a permitted Canadian regulated bank or an authorized foreign dealer and the hedge is documented as cash-settled for currencies not freely deliverable in Canada
FX options (call and put) used for optional conversion of foreign-currency platform settlement proceeds into CAD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Limited Partnership Annual Return (Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-13, Part 2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies / Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the LP registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 100 (approx. USD 73) late-filing penalty after the deadline; continued default triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution; reinstatement requires full arrears plus filing fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Food Premises Business Licence Annual Renewal (ghost kitchen facility)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: City of Calgary Licence & Business Services or City of Edmonton Business Licensing (per operating location)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the licence anniversary date; renewal filing accepted up to 60 days before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operation without a valid licence constitutes a municipal offence with escalating fines and potential closure order; delivery-platform payouts (UberEats/DoorDash) may be suspended upon proof of lapsed licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under Alberta partnership law; an independent audit is mandatory only if the LP is a reporting issuer or investment fund, if the partnership agreement or a lender requires it, if a municipal licence inspection demands audited statements, or if the CRA issues a formal audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private LPs; IFRS permitted if the entity or its general partner is publicly accountable; accrual-basis statements are required for Canadian tax and lending purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta imposes no annual UBO filing for LPs; however, a Beneficial Ownership Register must be maintained internally and updated within 15 days of any transfer of partnership interest. The register must be reviewed annually in tandem with the LP Annual Return, and the general partner must certify that registered office, general partner identity, and limited partner capital records are accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 - 300 per year (Alberta registered office / agent service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 8,500 per year (ASPE financial statement preparation and independent review/audit for a ghost kitchen LP)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Not applicable to a Canadian limited partnership (LP) that is treated as a partnership for Canadian income tax purposes. The LP generally computes income and allocates each partner’s share under the Income Tax Act; partners are taxed on their allocated shares. Alberta corporate income tax rates apply to taxable Alberta corporations, not to the LP as such.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The LP is generally a flow-through vehicle, not an entity eligible for a corporate tax holiday. Each partner may separately qualify for applicable deductions, credits, or incentives, subject to the relevant statutory conditions and allocation rules. No incentive should be assumed solely because the business operates as a ghost kitchen.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Not applicable as a five-year LP-level rule. Partnership losses are generally allocated to partners under the Income Tax Act and may be limited by partner-level rules, including at-risk rules for limited partners. A partner’s allowable non-capital loss is generally subject to the partner-level carryforward rules; for losses arising after 2005, the general carryforward period is 20 taxation years. Character and use restrictions apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013, Partnership Information Return, filed electronically through CRA-certified tax software or the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) My Business Account filing services where available. A partnership generally files only if it meets a CRA filing condition, including specified revenue, expense, asset, partner, or allocation criteria. Alberta does not impose a separate general partnership income tax return on an LP solely because it carries on business in Alberta.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, if a T5013 filing condition is met. The partnership’s fiscal period is generally its tax year; a fiscal period may not exceed 12 months. A partnership that is not required to file a T5013 may still have information, withholding, GST/HST, payroll, or other filing obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T5013 return and applicable partner slips are generally due five months after the partnership’s fiscal period-end. Separate deadlines apply to partners’ own income tax returns and to withholding remittances and information returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 return — partnership identification and fiscal period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the partnership’s legal name, business number, partnership account identifier where applicable, address, fiscal-period start and end dates, and principal business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the partnership’s Canadian business number and accurately identify its Canadian activities. A non-resident partner’s status does not remove the partnership’s filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 return — revenue, expenses, and net income or loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report partnership-level income and deductions using the applicable T5013 return schedules and tax classifications. Reconcile accounting results to amounts computed under the Income Tax Act; maintain records for delivery-platform settlements, refunds, commissions, food costs, rent, payroll, equipment, and related-party charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute Canadian-source income and any income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment or business activity under the applicable rules. Do not treat accounting profit or platform deposits as the tax allocation without reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 slips — partner identification and allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issue a T5013 slip to each partner and report the partner’s share of income, loss, deductions, credits, and other applicable amounts by character and source. Allocation must follow the partnership agreement and applicable tax law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the non-resident partner’s correct legal name, address, country of residence, and tax identification details where required. Determine Canadian-source amounts and applicable withholding separately; a T5013 slip does not itself discharge withholding duties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File Form T106, Information Return of Non-Arm’s Length Transactions with Non-Residents, when the statutory reporting threshold and conditions are met. Report relevant transactions and balances with non-resident related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the CAD 1 million reporting threshold to the aggregate reportable transactions under the applicable T106 rules. The threshold is a reporting test, not a transfer-pricing exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File NR4 information returns and remit Part XIII withholding where amounts subject to Canadian non-resident withholding are paid or credited. Other regimes, including Regulation 105 withholding for services rendered in Canada, may apply independently.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the beneficial recipient, income character, Canadian source, applicable statutory rate, and treaty eligibility before payment or credit. Obtain valid treaty documentation and remit withholding by the applicable due date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A late T5013 filing can attract a penalty generally calculated at CAD 25 per day, subject to a CAD 100 minimum and CAD 2,500 maximum under the applicable late-information-return rules; higher penalties may apply for repeated or intentional non-compliance. Separate penalties and interest may apply to incorrect or missing slips, failure to withhold or remit, failure to file T106, inaccurate reporting, and unpaid tax. CRA may assess interest at prescribed rates. The precise penalty depends on the statutory provision and facts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: A partnership distribution is not, merely by being distributed, a dividend paid by a corporation. A non-resident partner is generally taxed on allocated partnership income under the applicable Canadian rules; withholding depends on the income’s character and source. If a Canadian corporation separately pays a dividend to a non-resident, the general Part XIII rate is 25%, subject to reduction under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Confirm the recipient’s residence, beneficial ownership, income classification, and entitlement under the relevant Canadian income tax treaty. Obtain a valid certificate of residence or other acceptable tax-residency evidence and the applicable CRA treaty-relief declaration or prescribed supporting documentation before applying a reduced rate. For dividends, interest, and royalties, use the applicable CRA forms and payer procedures, including NR301 where appropriate; retain supporting records and apply withholding at the domestic rate if treaty entitlement is not adequately established. Treaty relief is treaty-specific and may be limited by beneficial-ownership, limitation-on-benefits, principal-purpose, or other anti-abuse provisions. A certificate of residence alone does not establish entitlement in every case.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Canadian Part XIII withholding rate is 25% on Canadian-source royalties and interest paid or credited to a non-resident, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty reductions. Interest paid to an arm’s-length non-resident is generally exempt from Part XIII withholding under the domestic rules, subject to exceptions, including participating debt interest and certain non-arm’s-length arrangements. Treaty rates vary by treaty, recipient, beneficial ownership, and payment type; no single treaty rate can be stated without identifying the recipient’s residence and the applicable treaty. Payments for services performed in Canada may instead trigger Regulation 105 withholding, generally 15% of gross fees, subject to waiver or reduction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada does not impose a universal Local File/Master File filing threshold of the type used in some jurisdictions. Contemporaneous documentation under Income Tax Act section 247 is required for relevant non-arm’s-length cross-border transactions, with a statutory penalty safe-harbour condition generally tied to records being made by the documentation deadline and provided within three months of a CRA request. T106 reporting generally applies where its CAD 1 million aggregate transaction threshold and other conditions are met. Country-by-Country Reporting generally applies to a Canadian-resident ultimate parent or surrogate parent of an MNE group with consolidated group revenue of at least CAD 1.125 billion in the preceding fiscal year, subject to the statutory rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a general Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to the UAE ESR. Canadian tax consequences may nevertheless depend on the actual legal and economic arrangements, including transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, specific anti-avoidance provisions, beneficial ownership, treaty anti-abuse rules, and factual residence or permanent-establishment analysis. Maintain evidence that related-party charges reflect services actually performed and arm’s-length terms.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file partnership information returns or partner slips
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file a required T5013 return, issue accurate partner slips, or report partnership income and allocations by the applicable deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing and information-return penalties, reassessments, interest, and possible penalties for knowingly or negligently making false statements. The amount depends on the return, the number of slips, duration, and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: An LP has a general partner rather than corporate directors as its managing person. The general partner may face contractual, statutory, or tax-related liability according to its legal form and the facts. Limited partners are not automatically liable for partnership tax debts merely because they are partners, but their protection depends on applicable Alberta law and their conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold or remit non-resident tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying or crediting Canadian-source dividends, royalties, taxable interest, or other amounts to a non-resident without applying required withholding, or failing to remit amounts withheld.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unremitted withholding, interest, and penalties under the Income Tax Act. Treaty relief does not excuse failure to establish entitlement or meet applicable administrative requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the payer is a corporation, director liability for unremitted source deductions may arise under statutory conditions, including due diligence defences. An LP’s general partner or responsible persons may face liability under the applicable statutory and entity rules. Criminal liability requires the relevant statutory elements and proof.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm’s-length cross-border prices or allocations that do not satisfy the arm’s-length principle, or failing to maintain and provide required contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust income, impose interest, and assess a transfer-pricing penalty generally equal to 10% of the applicable net transfer-pricing adjustment where statutory thresholds and conditions are met. Treaty and competent-authority procedures may be available to address double taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: No automatic veil-piercing or imprisonment arises solely from a transfer-pricing adjustment. Personal exposure requires a separate statutory basis or evidence of conduct meeting the elements of a civil or criminal offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion, false statements, or deliberate concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly concealing sales, fabricating expenses, falsifying partner allocations, maintaining false books, or intentionally evading tax or withholding obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties, interest, reassessment beyond ordinary limitation periods in specified circumstances, and prosecution may apply. Tax evasion on conviction can result in fines of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to five years under the Income Tax Act; additional offences and sanctions may apply on the facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A general partner, officer, or other individual may be prosecuted where the statutory elements and evidence establish personal participation or authorization. Imprisonment is not automatic; civil restitution, travel bans, and veil-piercing are not automatic tax penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undisclosed permanent establishment or Canadian business activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating a non-resident partner’s Canadian business income as exempt without analyzing Canadian source, carrying on business, permanent establishment, and applicable treaty rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of Canadian tax, interest, failure-to-file penalties, and possible withholding or information-reporting liabilities may result. Treaty relief depends on the relevant treaty and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: No automatic personal liability follows solely from a permanent-establishment finding. Liability requires an applicable statutory basis, such as a director-liability provision, or personal involvement in an offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported sales, payroll, GST/HST, or platform settlement discrepancies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting delivery-platform sales, misclassifying marketplace fees, failing to register or remit GST/HST when required, or failing to meet payroll withholding and reporting obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessments for tax, GST/HST, source deductions, interest, and applicable penalties may apply. GST/HST registration and collection obligations depend on the taxable supplies, registration thresholds, and business facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a corporate general partner may be subject to statutory liability for specified unremitted amounts if the legal conditions are met. For an LP, exposure depends on the general partner’s legal form, the applicable statute, and the individual’s conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, proceeds of crime, or deceptive ownership and payment flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly handling criminal proceeds, disguising beneficial ownership, using false invoices, or routing funds to conceal their source or destination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code offences may result in significant fines, forfeiture, and imprisonment, depending on the offence and circumstances. FINTRAC obligations apply only to persons and activities covered by the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; a ghost-kitchen operator is not automatically a reporting entity solely because it accepts delivery-platform payouts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals may be prosecuted for personal participation, authorization, or other conduct meeting the offence elements. A corporate role alone does not establish criminal liability; travel restrictions and imprisonment require lawful process and applicable statutory grounds.
